- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak or use 2-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) or shows strong reversal signals, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% buffer to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model exhibits strong lag in correcting downward trends; if 3+ consecutive days show falling prices, adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lagged mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; apply exponential decay weighting (e.g., 0.8 decay factor) to recent history to reduce noise amplification.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model tends to err on the side of overconfidence; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5-day mean to anchor forecast.
